title: In 16 larval zebrafish, regions with shorter projectome walks to swim motor regions encode swimming more (rho -0.56), but rostro-caudal position explains this; it is not specific to motor targets
abstract: Question: in C. elegans, neurons with a shorter connectome random walk to muscle encode locomotion more strongly. Does this rule apply to a vertebrate brain at region scale? Data: whole-brain two-photon calcium imaging of larval zebrafish with tail tracking (Legare et al. 2025, CC BY 4.0; 16 fish with 10 or more swim bouts) and the 70-region directed mapZebrain projectome. Method: we hashed the plan before we computed a structure-encoding statistic. Swim encoding per neuron was the cross-validated ridge R2 of lagged swim vigour beyond dark-flash terms; region encoding was the mean over neurons, then the median over fish. H_out was the random-walk hitting time from a region to the swim motor set (nMLF and ventral medulla). Results: rho(H_out, encoding) was -0.56 (60 regions, p = 3e-6), negative in 15 of 16 fish, stronger than 1,000 strength-preserving rewired graphs (p = 0.001) and stable after control for Euclidean distance and signal covariates (partial rho -0.64). By the pre-set rule, H1 was supported. But rewired graphs that keep edge lengths gave the same relation (null mean -0.50, p = 0.14), the eye-motor control set gave -0.50, and the retina gave +0.46. Post hoc, the rostro-caudal coordinate alone gave -0.67; after control for it, H_out gave -0.14 (p = 0.28). Random 4-region hindbrain target sets gave the same rho as the motor set (mean -0.54). Inside the hindbrain the relation was absent. In 31 midbrain and forebrain regions, H_out predicted encoding beyond the rostro-caudal coordinate (-0.57), but random hindbrain sets and jittered motor sets did equally well. Only the input route from the motor set (H_in) was specific outside the hindbrain (partial rho -0.40, p = 0.024; post hoc). Conclusion: the raw worm relation repeats, but geometry and the hindbrain concentration of swim encoding explain it at this scale. Limitations: region-scale dense projectome from other animals; 1 Hz imaging; post-hoc controls; the planned fly test failed because the Dryad download was refused.

display.caption: (A) Region swim encoding against projectome random-walk steps to the swim motor set (orange: hindbrain). (B) Nulls: strength-preserving rewiring, edge-length-preserving rewiring and random hindbrain target sets. (C) Rho for target sets and measures with 95% fish-bootstrap intervals. (D) Post-hoc spatial controls: the relation disappears after control for rostro-caudal position and inside the hindbrain.
Dorsal view of region centroids: (A) swim encoding is concentrated in the caudal hindbrain; (B) projectome distance to the motor set (orange squares) is short in most of the hindbrain.
